brief.topic: Measuring AI adoption by licenses issued
brief.audience: Leaders and PMs running enterprise AI rollouts
constraints: Illustrative numbers labelled on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Licences, logins and prompt counts measure access, not adoption; report weekly use on real work, measurable task impact and repeat use instead.

hooks.text: Licenses issued is not AI adoption.
hooks.notes: Names the exact number on most rollout dashboards; clear in under two seconds.

hooks.text: Your AI rollout dashboard is measuring the wrong thing.
hooks.notes: Intriguing but vague until the reel explains which thing.

hooks.text: 5,000 seats. How many people actually changed how they work?
hooks.notes: Strong question, but the number would have to be labelled illustrative in the hook itself.

selectionRationale: Highest total (24/25). It challenges a metric leaders actually report, which makes it shareable inside rollout teams, and the reel replaces it with three better measures.

scenes.purpose: Challenge the most common rollout metric.
scenes.onScreen: Licenses issued is not adoption. / Measure this instead.
scenes.voiceover: Licenses issued is not AI adoption.

storyboard.animation: Readable on frame 0; underline sweep; sub at 18.

scenes.purpose: Show the numbers that usually get reported.
scenes.onScreen: WHAT GETS REPORTED / Easy to count. Says little. / Licenses assigned · Logins this month · Prompts sent
scenes.voiceover: Licenses assigned, logins, prompts sent. Easy to count. They say little.

scenes.purpose: Replace each vanity metric with one that shows real use and value.
scenes.onScreen: WHAT SHOWS VALUE / Count use on real work. / ADOPTION weekly users on a real task · IMPACT tasks done faster or better · RETENTION repeat use after week 4
scenes.voiceover: Instead, count weekly users on a real task, tasks done faster or better, and people still using it after week four.

storyboard.visual: Same stack (hard cut); each card flips to a green metric.

swap.text: Weekly users on a real task

scenes.purpose: Make the difference tangible with a clearly labelled illustration.
scenes.onScreen: SAME ROLLOUT [ILLUSTRATIVE] / Seats with a license 100% / Weekly use on real work 18% / Report the second number.
scenes.voiceover: In this illustrative example, every seat has a license, but only eighteen percent use it weekly on real work. Report the second number.

storyboard.visual: ILLUSTRATIVE badge; neutral 100% bar vs amber 18% bar; conclusion.
storyboard.animation: Left at 4, right at 30 with count-up; conclusion at 84.

scenes.purpose: Memorable rule + share CTA aimed at rollout teams.
scenes.onScreen: Count use, not licenses. / Share this with your AI rollout team
scenes.voiceover: Count use, not licenses. Share this with your AI rollout team.

storyboard.visual: Two-line takeaway; arrow CTA; end card.
storyboard.animation: Lines rise; CTA at 40; end card at 70.

scenes.cta: Share this with your AI rollout team

caption.opening: A licence tells you someone can use the tool. It doesn’t tell you they do — or that it helps.
body:
Common rollout metrics measure access:
→ licences assigned
→ logins this month
→ prompts sent

Better signals of adoption and value:
→ weekly users on a real, named task
→ tasks done faster or better (pick one task, measure before and after)
→ people still using it after week four
(The 100% vs 18% in the reel is an illustrative example, not data from a real organisation.)
caption.cta: Share this with your AI rollout team.

primaryCta.text: Share this with your AI rollout team

claims.text: Licence counts, logins and prompt volumes measure access rather than adoption or value.
100% of seats licensed vs 18% weekly use on real work.

carousel: 3/ Adoption: weekly use on a real task
5/ Retention: still using it after week 4
repurposing.followUpReel: Format 2 (Framework): how to measure task impact in a two-week before/after test.
repurposing.linkedin: Post for rollout leads: replace three vanity metrics with three adoption metrics; ask which one their dashboard shows today.
